title: Transparent, Translucent & Opaque
keyIdea: Materials treat light in three ways. Transparent materials let you see clearly through them. Translucent materials let some light through but the view is blurry. Opaque materials block light so you cannot see through them.
familyTip: Shine a torch through clear plastic, tissue paper and a book. Ask: 'Can you see the torch shape clearly, only a glow, or nothing?' Sort three more household materials the same way.

visual.caption: Light through materials — fair idea or myth? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: opaque means you can read through it

lab.caption: Flagship lab: shine through clear, frosted and card; sort three classes; predict wood; then challenge.

kid: Transparent means you can see clearly through it.
Translucent means some light gets through, but it looks blurry.
Opaque means the light is blocked. You cannot see through it.
Test with a torch: clear view, blurry glow, or no light past.
adult: KS1 science: light and materials. Words: transparent, translucent, opaque, beam, torch, clear, blurry, block.
Common mistakes: calling every clear-looking thing transparent; mixing translucent with opaque; thinking opaque means you can still read through it; skipping a torch test.
In the lab your child shines through glass, tissue and card, sorts all three, predicts wood is opaque, then tries challenge traps for those slips.
